title: Autotune: Default batching/caching + quant profiles + unit-econ tooling
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Context: This PR implements the first iteration of the autotune pipeline that recommends and applies cost-optimized defaults for batching and prefix/KV caching, ships quantization profile support for model variants, and adds initial unit-economics (uecon) tooling in the Console to help customers visualize expected token cost savings. Motivation: recurring customer feedback + internal benchmarks show 20-50% per-token cost delta across workloads when batching/caching defaults and quant profiles are tuned. We want a small-footprint, opt-in automation that suggests defaults and exposes the expected unit-econ impact before committing. This change bundles three coordinated pieces: 1) runtime/autotune: autotuner service that collects per-route telemetry (latency, seq-length dist, qps), simulates batching/caching profiles and recommends defaults; 2) runtime/quant: quantization profile loader and compatibility checks so the router can fall back to compatible quantized variants; 3) console/uecon: a new UEcon dashboard and tooling to preview cost impact for a route and apply recommendations. Checklist: - [x] Telemetry collection hooks added to router and batcher - [x] Autotune simulation engine + planner - [x] Quant profile schema + compatibility checks - [x] Console UI for preview + apply flow - [x] End-to-end integration tests - [x] Docs and changelog entry Summary of commits: - feat(autotune): add planner and simulation microbench (3e4a2f) - feat(runtime): add batching defaults heuristic and KV cache tuning (b9c7d1) - feat(quant): quant profile loader + model metadata enriched (f2a9b0) - feat(console): uecon preview page and apply endpoint (5d1e88) - fix(tests): stabilize e2e perf test harness (a07c3b) Changed areas (high level): - runtime/autotune/{planner,scheduler}.py: simulation and candidate scoring - runtime/batcher: default policy implementation and exposure via config - runtime/kv_cache: TTL/eviction defaults adjusted and metrics - runtime/quant: profile schema, loader, and compatibility checks - console/uecon: front-end routes, backend endpoints, and webhook for apply flow - docs: autotune and uecon usage guide - tests/e2e: new scenarios and perf assertions Review and discussion: - Daniel Kim (reviewer): "Can the planner be limited to X% of requests for the first rollout to avoid instability in production?" Author reply: "Yes
 added a rollout_fraction param and defaulted to 5% in runtime config; will increase after validation." - Priya Rao: "The simulation currently assumes uniform batch arrival; can we use the observed inter-arrival distribution instead?" Author reply: "Good catch
 planner now samples from observed inter-arrival histograms (configurable backfill)." - Marcus Li: "Quant profile compatibility needs a deterministic fallback. What happens on mismatch?" Author reply: "Router will fall back to the nearest compatible variant and record a metric (quant.incompatible_fallback). Added tests to cover both paths." CI and testing: Initial CI run showed a flaky e2e perf test (tests/e2e/test_batching_latency.py::test_latency_under_load) failing due to ephemeral env noise; added retry logic and tuned harness to be deterministic. Final CI status: all checks passed (unit, lint, e2e, perf smoke). Merge notes: squashed and merged to main after approvals from Daniel, Priya, and Marcus. Rollout: autotune is behind a feature flag (autotune.enabled=false by default); UEcon Console pages are feature-gated to internal tenants until we validate telemetry for 2 weeks. Linked tasks: ENG-1209 (autotune core), ENG-1253 (uecon console); no Jira links for this change. Release notes: "Adds autotune pipeline that suggests cost-optimized batching and KV-cache defaults, introduces quantization profile support for model variants, and adds a UEcon preview page in Console to visualize cost impact. Feature gated and off by default."

release_notes: - New: Autotune planner that recommends batching and KV-cache defaults. - New: Quantization profile support and compatibility checks for model variants. - New: UI: UEcon preview and apply flow in Console (feature-gated). - Change: Default rollout fraction set to 5% to limit initial exposure.
notes: Operational notes: enable autotune.enabled=true and configure autotune.rollout_fraction and autotune.data_retention_days. Monitor metrics: autotune.recommendation_accepted, quant.incompatible_fallback, uecon.preview_savings. If you see high latency regressions after acceptance, disable autotune.rollout_fraction and investigate per-route planner logs.
